deep.reconstruction:
This page is not mathematics. It is a set of instrument-calibration notes on a Charles Chevalier (Paris) compound microscope, apparently made with a view to micrometric measurement. The quantities and what they serve are as follows.

(1) Rack and screws.
- Rack pitch ('Zähne der Stange'): 1 tooth = 1.585 mm.
- Vertical (focusing) screw: 1 thread = 0.428 mm.
- Stage screw ('Porte-objet Schraube', acting normal to the tube): 1 thread = 0.4443 mm.

(2) Focusing positions of the objective combinations. The detachable lenses A, B, C can be combined. The settings are read in screw turns relative to AC = 0:
- ABC: 0.5
- AB: 8.28 (second reading 8.68)
- BC: 8.7(7?)
- B: 13.8
- A: 23.6
Converting to mm with 0.428 mm/turn (my step): ABC ≈ 0.21 mm, AB ≈ 3.54 (3.71) mm, BC ≈ 3.75 mm, B ≈ 5.91 mm, A ≈ 10.10 mm. These are the differences in focusing height, i.e. relative working distances; the weaker single lenses focus farther away.

(3) Field of view with the cylindrical tube attached, measured in 1/40 English inch:
- Ocular 1 / Obj. 1: 4.9 parts, which is 4.9·25.4/40 ≈ 3.11 mm (my conversion).
- Obj. 2: 2.6 parts, marked '?' (≈1.65 mm).
- Obj. 1.2: 1.2 parts = 0.77 mm 'on the scale'. Check: 1.2·25.4/40 = 0.762 mm, consistent with Gauss's 0.77.

(4) Cylindrical tube removed, Oc. 1 Obj. 1.
- 'Vergrößerung = 1/8.2 mm' and 'Gesichtsfeld = 1/2.2' when the eyepiece tube is fully pushed in.
- 'Vergrößerung = 1/5.5 mm' when the eyepiece is drawn out 99.5 mm.
The magnification seems to be recorded as the object length (1/8.2 mm, resp. 1/5.5 mm) corresponding to a fixed image unit. Drawing the tube out 99.5 mm therefore raises the magnification by a factor of about 8.2/5.5 ≈ 1.49.

(5) Field of view (mm) as a function of draw-tube extension (mm). This calibrates field against extension; it continues on the next page for 1.2 and the new Repsold objective.
- Obj. 2: 0.80 at 99.5; 0.99 at 40; 1.1 at 0.
- Obj. 3: 0.965 at 99.5.
- Obj. 4: 0.895 at 99.5; 0.95 at 80; 0.985 at 70.
The field decreases monotonically as the tube is drawn out, as expected because magnification rises. No derivation or theory is present.
errors: No mathematical errors. Small internal inconsistency: 1.2/40 inch = 0.762 mm, while Gauss writes 0.77 mm; this is within reading precision.
Two readings for AB (8.28 and 8.68) and an overwritten digit for BC indicate that the measurements were repeated or corrected; the value for Obj. 2 (2.6) is itself queried by Gauss with '?'.

results.what: Calibration of microscope screws (thread pitch in mm), objective focusing offsets, field of view and magnification versus draw-tube extension for a Chevalier microscope
results.modern_name: instrument calibration / micrometry of a compound microscope

deep.surprise_reason: Purely practical calibration data for a commercial microscope (Chevalier, plus a Repsold objective on the next page); no mathematics. Gauss's interest in optical instruments is well known.

checkable.asserts: 1.2 parts of 1/40 inch = 0.762 mm, close to Gauss's 0.77 mm
Field 4.9/40 inch for Oc.1/Obj.1 equals about 3.11 mm
Focusing offset of lens A = 23.6 turns × 0.428 mm ≈ 10.10 mm
Focusing offset of lens B ≈ 5.906 mm
Magnification gain from drawing the eyepiece out 99.5 mm ≈ 1.49

transcription_corrections: 'Portoobject Schraube Normal gegen Rohr' = 'Porte-objet Schraube' (stage screw), acting normal to the tube.
Obj. 2 field entry reads '2,6' (the 2 is written over a 1), followed by Gauss's '?'.
BC value is '8,7?' with the last digit overwritten; 8.77 is uncertain.
'::' and '—' in the extension column are ditto marks.
Header reads 'Zähne der Stange 1^mm585' (rack tooth pitch).
A word before 'Objective' is struck through/smudged and illegible.
